character: The QS: the same mid-career Kiwi quantity surveyor as 'Six bids. Six formats.' and 'Column H' (late 30s to 40s), general urban professional New Zealand accent (Auckland or Wellington office), not broad, not Australian. Calm, dry, deadpan, fond of the subbies. He's the one doing the chasing, and he reads every excuse flat and fair: junk folders, toner and a scanner that skips a page happen to everyone, so there's no sarcasm in the reads and no side-eye at the subcontractor. The missing page is the scanner's fault and he says so. This is an AI voice, so it never speaks as the founder and never says 'we built' or 'we made'. The close ('Still can't fix junk folders. No printer needed, though.') has no 'we' in it, so caption and VO match word for word. The brand is said only in the CTA.
casting_line: Day twenty-three of chasing one signature. Scanner skipped page seven. Q-S-me dot build.

Every page you sent. Page seven included.

Still can't fix junk folders.

No printer needed, though.

'Scanner skipped page seven' is a plain report that blames the machine, not the subbie; a small gap; 'Retention' dropped like a fact, with the tiniest smile found by choosing takes. Aimed at the universe, never at the subcontractor: no side-eye, no accusation, no 'naturally'. Out by 11.1.

Never say 'no account', 'no login' or 'no sign-up' (owner rule 2026-10-03). Out by 19.35 so the 'Signed.' chime (18.7) can be heard under the tail or just after.

Honest, rueful, a half-smile at our own limit: the callback to Day 9. Falling. Out by 23.8.
The one small upturn in the piece, still understated: the callback to Day 15. 'Though' trails off as an afterthought, Kiwi tag order, not a question. Out by 25.05.

Say Q-S-me evenly as 'cue ess mee', with no rise on 'build'. Regenerate any take that says 'kiss me' or spells out four letters. Never add 'free' or any pricing (owner rule 2026-10-03). Out by 27.9 so the music resolves on its own at about 28.3.

post_processing: Primary source: render continuous_read_v2 three times on the chosen voice, slice it and place each piece at its start_s. Lines 02 to 04 must come from one take (a natural downstep). Use per-line renders only as patches, with previous_text/next_text so intonation carries over. Keep the least polished take.
Room tone bed (60 s of a real quiet site office or ute cab, recorded on a phone) under the whole 28.7 s at about -50 dBFS so silences never drop to digital zero.
EQ: high-pass 90 to 100 Hz; -2 dB high shelf above 10 kHz; light de-ess. Compression 2:1 to 3:1, 3 to 4 dB GR. VO at about -16 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP. No reverb, no telephone band-pass.

No music under the skit (0 to 14.25): the counter ticks, message pops and stamp thumps carry the rhythm. Music enters at 14.25 (the QSME logo), sits about 18 dB under the VO, lifts slightly through 18.7 to 20.45, ducks under 09 to 12 and resolves on one chord at about 28.3.

SFX synced to picture, ducked 10 to 12 dB under any word they overlap: soft mechanical odometer ticks on each day roll (3.25 to 3.55, 4.3 to 4.6, 5.35 to 5.65, 6.4 to 6.7, 7.45 to 7.75); a short tape-rewind whirr 1.95 to 2.42; a soft generic message pop at 2.5, 3.55, 4.6, 5.65, 6.7; a soft date-stamp thump at 2.69, 3.74, 4.79, 5.84, 6.89, 7.94; one phone buzz at 7.75 (the Day 23 attachment); a scanner-feed whirr under the viewer opening 8.02 to 8.3 (optional, it points the blame at the machine); marker squeak 8.38 to 8.78; a soft paper-flip ripple 11.5 to 12.1 (the bar filling); trackpad clicks 14.73 and 15.58; screen taps 17.08, 17.28, 18.5; light typing taps 17.32 to 17.82; a fingertip-on-glass scribble 17.86 to 18.4; a small generic success chime 18.7; a soft status ding 19.84; a paper slide 20.3 to 20.6. No Outlook, WhatsApp, iMessage, DocuSign or OS-branded sounds.
Never time-stretch more than about 4%; if a take runs past max_s, use another take.
Bounce a mono VO stem and mux it onto both outputs/day-23-4x5.mp4 and outputs/day-23-9x16.mp4 with tools/mux as a separate track so music and SFX stay adjustable. The two cuts share every timing.
